newsitem.title: UK: EU Commission to trim German deficit forecast - paper.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission to trim German deficit forecast - paper.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to reduce its forecast for Germany's 1997 budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product, the British weekly newspaper the Observer reported on Sunday.

The new forecast, due on Wednesday, is down from forecasts leaked last week of 3.2 percent and equals the Maastricht Treaty requirement for membership of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) due to start in January 1999.

The Observer said the new forecast would also put France's deficit/GDP ratio at three percent and would indicate that most European Union countries would qualify for the launch of the European single currency.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday that Germany would fulfil the convergence criteria for EMU participation, though much budget consolidation was still needed.
But German media said last week the spring report by the country's six leading economic research institutes, due on Tuesday, will forecast a public-sector deficit of 3.2 percent for 1997.
